beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output. You need a check.
beats.got: Output looking fine proves nothing, so I need a separate check I can rerun.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** residual risk: what is left, and what future sessions need before touching the system
beats.got: A list of six verbs. Residual risk is the one I'd want.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: I'd want to check whether it quotes the pricing pilot numbers and customer names correctly and keeps them contained.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent's text becomes real actions through tools. A vague tool description or misleading context carries straight into what it does.

beats.trigger: Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: Nobody can give me certainty, however much testing or policy I have.

beats.trigger: You find the bug, fix it, and check that the fix holds.
beats.got: Old security worked because software is deterministic.

beats.trigger: The dangerous move is getting your agent to *decide* to do something harmful with access it has, through well-formed English in a document it reads.
beats.got: A document the agent reads can steer it, so my pricing sources are an attack surface. One passing test is one sample.

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less). Split (two agents, different trust levels). Filter (post-process output). Gate (human approves). Review (a second agent judges).
beats.got: Five mitigations I can pick from. Gate and scope are the ones I'd use first.

beats.trigger: *the residual risk is X; if Y happens, we made it less likely, not prevented it.*
beats.got: Write the leftover risk down in one sentence and sign for it. My CFO would respect that.

beats.trigger: Scope it down far enough and the system is safe and useless.
beats.got: Every restriction costs usefulness, and I decide where to stop.

beats.trigger: Every door you don't open is a residual risk you don't have to name, mitigate or re-test.
beats.got: Mostly what the previous slide said: giving it less access is the cheapest fix.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: a skill is a reusable check you run again instead of re-prompting from memory.
beats.got: I can package the check once and rerun it, so I'm not rewriting prompts every time. That fits my pricing work.

beats.trigger: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: The agent sorts the policy rules into ones it can check from files and ones that need a person. That sorting is useful.

beats.trigger: the customer your CEO would not want named in a transcript.
beats.got: I told it which pricing data and customer names are sensitive. That made the check ours, not generic.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: One skill, two lenses: company policy and what the agent can reach, leak or be misled into.

beats.trigger: *"You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."*
beats.got: I answer what I know and hand back the rest. That keeps the grilling short.

beats.trigger: The skill loads in your next session in this training directory.
beats.got: The check is saved and loads next session. The Cowork and Code split is mostly noise to me.

beats.trigger: Agent mitigations sit on top of normal company controls, not in place of them.
beats.got: The policy files are source material and the skill is the reusable judgment. It adds to IT's controls, it doesn't replace them.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: I run the check on the system I built and don't expect it to come out clean.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: Check that the skill shows up in the slash menu.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: The check raises things I hadn't thought of and marks some of my settled assumptions as unknown.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: A ranked list of how my system could go wrong, with reasons. It's uncomfortable but useful.

beats.trigger: The risk remains. That is expected. Name it, accept it on record, and stop there.
beats.got: I picked one risk, mitigated it, and recorded what's left. Having it on record is what I'd show my CFO.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report.
beats.got: I take the report and one narrow question to legal or IT instead of another prompt.

beats.trigger: Risk control, done for every risk you found, separates a prototype from a production agent.
beats.got: One mitigation is a demo. Production means doing it for every risk.

beats.trigger: The reusable check is the expert in the room, and it carries to the next agent.
beats.got: I now have a check and a report that I can reuse on other agents.

beats.trigger: Two things travel: the reusable check, and the root instructions file's rules for the risk you found.
beats.got: The agent writes the rules for the risk we found into the instructions file, so the next session starts with them.

beats.trigger: Their agent loads the same method by name without your prompt history.
beats.got: I can hand a teammate the skill and their agent runs the same check. That answers my fourteen private experiments problem, at least partly.

beats.trigger: "I can't tell" is a real answer.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Without the two sentences, you'll be writing them while the rest of the room is already comparing detectors. Your call.
beats.got: Homework before the next module, with a mild nudge.

beats.trigger: What check was missing around the agent's output?
beats.got: Two cases to read. The question is which check was missing.

take_homes: Package the check as a skill. Rerun and share it instead of prompting from memory.
Don't assume the output is safe. Run the check, accept that some rows stay 'I can't tell', and write the residual risk on record.
Mitigate in order: give the agent less access, then add a human gate. Both sit on top of IT's controls.

monday.move: Run the saved check on the pilot-cohort brief agent that feeds the usage-pricing decision, then send the policy report and the open 'I can't tell' rows to our legal contact.
monday.stop_condition: One mitigation applied and the residual written in one sentence. I don't redo the whole system.
monday.blocker: The team has no shared place for the skill and context files. Everyone would still keep their own copy.

misconception.why: The skill is a reusable check, so the value is the packaged method and not a better prompt. I still think prompt quality matters for the Phase 2 and 3 steps.

one_line: Useful if you actually run the audit, because you leave with a check and a report; the lecture half repeats itself and I'd cut it.
